epic.intent:
Today a Dark Mechanicus folder is one Git repository: one project, one checkout, one epic branch, one Definition of Done. Many people keep their repositories side by side in one folder (for example `~/Documents/GitHub`), and real work often spans several of them. This epic lets a person open that parent folder, plan one epic across its repositories and run it, with every ticket saying which repository it changes.

## What changes
- **Setup.** A tracked folder that is not inside a Git repository and has child Git repositories offers **Folder of repositories**. It is always set up in the machine-local `db` storage mode (decision 0002): nothing is written into the parent folder or any child repository.
- **Repositories.** The immediate child folders that hold a `.git` directory or file are detected and recorded on the project under their exact folder names. Hidden and symlinked children and deeper repositories are skipped. **Rescan** adds new ones and marks vanished ones missing; it never drops one.
- **Tickets.** Every work ticket in a folder of repositories targets exactly one repository (new ticket field `repo`). The server keeps its title as `<exact folder name> - <description>`, for example `DarkMechanicus - Add refund endpoint`, and swaps the prefix when the repository changes. Acceptance nodes span repositories and carry neither. Single-repository folders refuse the field and are otherwise unchanged.
- **Planning.** `validate_plan` reports a work ticket without a repository, or naming one the project does not list. The planner guides split cross-repository work into one ticket per repository, wired with dependencies.
- **Runs.** The epic branch name is shared and bound in each repository the plan names, with that repository's own start commit. Packets give the worker the target repository's absolute path and branch. Each sprint's acceptance node lands one squashed increment per touched repository, each verified against that repository's history, and reports each touched repository's own Definition of Done.
- **Desktop.** Setup, a Repositories card with Rescan, a Repository picker in the ticket editor, the branch name at run start, and per-repository Definition of Done and increments.

## Contract (shared by the tickets)
- `project.json`: optional `repositories: RepositoryEntry[]`, with `RepositoryEntry = { name, missing?: true, definitionOfDone?: DefinitionOfDoneCheck[] }`. Its presence makes the project a folder of repositories. A repository's path is `<project root>/<name>`.
- `initialize_repository` gains `layout?: 'single' | 'multi_repo'` (default `single`). New command `rescan_repositories` (capability `project.repositories`).
- Ticket field `repo?: string` in `ticketContent`; `repo?: string | null` in `ticketInput` (`null` clears it in a patch).
- Title rule: exactly `${repo} - ${description}`, applied by the server.
- `WorkspaceCore.gitFor(repo: string | null): GitAdapter` (`null` is the project root, the single-repository case).
- Epic: `branch` keeps the shared name (`repository: null`, `startCommit: null`), and new `repositoryBranches?: EpicBranch[]` holds one entry per bound repository (`repository` is its name).
- Work packet `repository?: { name, path, branch }`. Acceptance packet `repositories?: { name, path, branch, definitionOfDone }[]` for the sprint's touched repositories.
- A sprint's **touched repositories** are the `repo` values of its work tickets with an accepted attempt.
- `incrementRef` gains `repo?`. In a folder of repositories, `submit_attempt` on an acceptance node takes `increments: IncrementRef[]` (one per touched repository) instead of `increment`, and `attempts.increment_json` then holds an array of verdicts, each with its `repo`.
- Definition of Done check names in evidence for a folder of repositories: `<repo>: <check name>`.

## Standards (owner decision, 2026-10-31)
Tests are listed and written in each ticket: every work ticket body has a **Tests** section, and testable behavior is written tests-first. There is no Fireguard ticket and no Fireguard run in this epic. The project's Definition of Done gates each sprint's acceptance node.

## Out of scope
- A Source control tab for a folder of repositories (the Source control epic is not on main).
- Repositories deeper than one level, submodules, and a parent folder that is itself inside a Git repository.
- `repo` storage mode for the parent folder, and converting an existing single-repository project.
- Retitling tickets when a child folder is renamed (rescan marks it missing and validation reports its tickets).
- A board filter by repository.

successCriteria.text: In the desktop app, adding a folder that is not a Git repository but holds child Git repositories offers Folder of repositories; after set-up the folder page lists every child repository by its exact folder name, and nothing was written into the parent folder or any child repository.

In a folder of repositories, a ticket targeting `DarkMechanicus` titled `Add refund endpoint` is stored and shown as `DarkMechanicus - Add refund endpoint`; moving it to another repository swaps the prefix; acceptance nodes carry no repository and no prefix.
`validate_plan` reports a work ticket without a repository or naming one the project does not list, and a single-repository project refuses the `repo` field.

A run of a two-repository epic hands each worker its repository's absolute path and epic branch, and a sprint passes only when each touched repository has a verified squashed increment and its own Definition of Done reported as passed.
Single-repository folders behave as before: their packets, increments, Definition of Done and titles are unchanged, and the existing suite passes.
The role guides, the orchestrator kickoff and the docs describe folders of repositories.

epic.title: Multi-repo folders: open a folder of Git repositories, target each ticket at one repository, and run epics across them

bundle.rationale:
## Decisions

The owner set these on 2026-10-31:
- **Storage:** a folder of repositories is always set up in the machine-local `db` storage mode. Nothing is written into the parent folder or any child repository.
- **Prefix:** the exact child folder name, as `<name> - <description>` (for example `DarkMechanicus - Add refund endpoint`). No humanizing and no display-name override.
- **Scope:** plan and execute across repositories in this epic.
- **Standards:** tests are listed and written in each ticket. No Fireguard ticket and no Fireguard run.

The planner assumed these (change them before Save if they are wrong):
- Repositories are the immediate children holding a `.git` directory or file. Hidden and symlinked children and deeper repositories are skipped. The parent must not be inside a Git repository.
- One work ticket targets exactly one repository; cross-repository changes are split and wired with dependencies. Acceptance nodes target none.
- The prefix is stored in the title and kept by the server, so every reader (board, CLI, search, the Linear transfer, commit messages) sees it. The `repo` field is the source of truth; the editor edits only the description.
- Ticket keys stay one sequence per project, with the key prefix derived from the parent folder's name as today.
- One shared epic branch name, bound per repository with its own start commit: the commit of that branch when it already exists in the repository, else the repository's current HEAD (the same rule a single repository uses today). The run binds every repository the saved plan names, and a repository first named in an adopted revision when it is adopted.
- A folder of repositories is in `db` mode, so no branch guard watches the child checkouts. The orchestrator guide therefore forbids switching a child repository's own checkout and does all integration in worktrees.
- In a folder of repositories each repository has its own Definition of Done, and there is no folder-level list.
- Rescan never drops a repository. A vanished one is marked missing and validation reports its tickets.

## Open questions
- Should a folder of repositories also allow folder-level Definition of Done checks next to the per-repository ones?
- The Source control epic (`ep_01m43sbb2tbnxtr35fety5vzhs`, not on main) will need to choose a child repository for a folder of repositories.

## Shape

One sprint ending in one human checkpoint. The owner compressed the original three sprints into one on 2026-10-31; the dependency edges keep their order inside it:
1. **Plan across repositories** (DM-345 to DM-352). Detection, set-up and the project record first, then the ticket field with its server-kept prefix. Validation, the planner guides and the editor build on the field; the set-up screen and the Repositories card build on the project record.
2. **Execute across repositories in the core** (DM-353 to DM-359). Per-repository Git adapters, then branch binding, then packets; increment verification runs beside packets, and the gate, views and records follow it; per-repository Definition of Done follows packets. A two-repository end-to-end integration test joins them.
3. **Agents and the desktop** (DM-360 to DM-363). Role guides and the kickoff, the branch name at run start, per-repository checks and increments in the app, then the docs.

One acceptance node (DM-342) runs the Definition of Done once on the combined work and verifies every ticket. Compressing removes the checkpoints between the parts, so the data-model decisions of part 1 are reviewed by a person only at the final checkpoint, after the execution work has built on them.

Concurrency is capped at 2: most tickets in a row touch shared core modules.

exitCriteria.text: A folder of repositories is set up from the desktop app without writing into the parent or any child repository, and its repositories are listed and rescanned.
Tickets in a folder of repositories carry a repository and a prefixed title, set from the editor or any command, and validate_plan reports missing or unknown repositories.
A run in a folder of repositories binds the epic branch per repository and hands each worker its repository's path and branch.
A sprint passes only when each touched repository has a verified squashed increment and reports its Definition of Done checks as passed.
An orchestrator started from the desktop app on a folder of repositories works each ticket in its own repository.
The desktop app shows Definition of Done checks and increments per repository, and the docs describe folders of repositories.
Single-repository folders, their tickets, runs, packets, increments and Definition of Done are unchanged.

tickets.body:
Run the project's Definition of Done once on the combined work in the sprint integration worktree. There is no Fireguard run in this epic. Then verify each covered item with the evidence its criterion names, land the sprint as one squashed commit on the epic branch, and submit that increment.

Fixtures: a scratch parent folder holding three scratch Git repositories (`alpha`, `beta`, and `gamma`, where `gamma` has a `.git` file because it was made with `git worktree add`), a plain folder, a symlink to `alpha` and a nested repository under the plain folder, and a scratch `DARKMECHANICUS_HOME`. The execution criteria (c9 to c15) and the agent and desktop criteria (c16 to c19) need only `alpha` and `beta`. Never open the live `state.sqlite` of the main checkout.

Where a criterion needs commands, run them through a throwaway in-process script (`openWorkspace` from `src/core/workspace.ts` against the scratch home), redact claim tokens in printed packets, and delete the script afterwards. Take screenshots from the built app (`npm run build`) started with the scratch `DARKMECHANICUS_HOME`. For the live orchestrator check, use a two-ticket fixture epic (one ticket per repository), start it from the built app, and stop the chat after its first accepted ticket.

reasoning.rationale: Verifies the sprint's combined work end to end on scratch repositories.

tickets.title: Sprint 1 acceptance

acceptanceCriteria.text: `detectChildRepos` returns only immediate, non-hidden, non-symlinked child directories that hold a `.git` directory or file, by exact name in code-point order.
`isInsideGitRepository` is true inside a Git work tree and false for a plain folder.
The listed tests in `childRepos.test.ts` pass, and lint and typecheck pass.

tickets.body:
**Context**
A folder of repositories is a parent folder whose immediate children are Git repositories. Nothing detects them today. The core filesystem port `FsAdapter` (`src/core/repo/types.ts`) already has `readdir`, `realpath`, `isSymlink`, `isDirectory` and `exists`.

**Change**
Add the module `src/core/repo/childRepos.ts`:
- `detectChildRepos(root: string, fs: FsAdapter): string[]` returns the names of the immediate children of `root` that are real directories (not symlinks) holding a `.git` entry, which may be a directory or a file (a worktree or submodule checkout has a `.git` file). Skip names starting with `.`. Return exact folder names sorted by code point. Never look below one level.
- `isInsideGitRepository(root: string, fs: FsAdapter): boolean` is true when `root` or any ancestor holds a `.git` entry. Follow the bounded ancestor walk in `src/core/repo/discovery.ts` (`findRepositoryRoot`, `MAX_ANCESTORS`).

**Out of scope**
Recording repositories on the project (next ticket), the desktop and any UI.

**Tests** (written first, in `src/core/repo/childRepos.test.ts`, with real temp directories)
- A parent with `alpha/.git/` (directory), `beta/.git` (file), `plain/`, a file `notes.txt`, `.hidden/.git/`, a symlink `linked -> alpha`, and `gamma/nested/.git/` returns exactly `['alpha', 'beta']`.
- An empty parent returns `[]`.
- `isInsideGitRepository` is true for a subfolder of a repository and false for a plain temp folder.

**Verify**
`npx vitest run src/core/repo/childRepos.test.ts`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: One pure module with spelled-out rules and tests.

tickets.title: Detect a folder's child Git repositories

acceptanceCriteria.text: `initialize_repository` with `layout: 'multi_repo'` sets the folder up in db mode, records its child repositories, and writes nothing into the parent or any child.
Set-up is refused for `mode: 'repo'`, a parent inside a Git repository, and a parent without child repositories, each with `invalid_input`.
`rescan_repositories` adds new repositories, marks vanished ones missing without removing them, and is refused for single-repository projects and for readers.
`get_project` returns `repositories` (null for a single repository), and a `project.json` without the field re-serializes unchanged.
The listed tests pass, and lint and typecheck pass.

tickets.body:
**Context**
`initialize_repository` (`src/core/commands/repository.ts`, schema `COMMAND_SCHEMAS.initializeRepository` in `src/core/commandSchemas.ts`) runs `initializeRepository` and `createProject` in `src/core/repo/initialize.ts`. The project record is `projectRecord` in `src/core/repo/portable.ts`; optional fields such as `definitionOfDone` have no default, so older records parse and re-serialize unchanged. `writeDefinitionOfDone` in `src/core/repo/projectConfig.ts` is the model for rewriting `project.json` in either storage mode. `get_project` returns `ProjectView` (`src/shared/domain/views.ts`). Child detection is `detectChildRepos` and `isInsideGitRepository` in `src/core/repo/childRepos.ts`.

**Change**
1. `projectRecord` gains optional `repositories: RepositoryEntry[]` (no default), with `RepositoryEntry = { name, missing?: true }`. A name is 1 to 255 characters with no `/`, `\` or NUL and is not `.` or `..`; names are unique. The field's presence, even when every repository is missing, marks a folder of repositories. Mirror it in `ProjectView` as `repositories: RepositoryView[] | null` (`null` for a single repository).
2. `initialize_repository` gains `layout?: 'single' | 'multi_repo'`. With `multi_repo` it:
   - refuses `mode: 'repo'` (`invalid_input`: a folder of repositories is stored in the database only), and uses `db` when the mode is omitted;
   - refuses a root inside a Git repository and a root with no child repositories, each with `invalid_input` and a message naming the folder;
   - records the detected repositories.
3. New command `rescan_repositories` (no input; new capability `project.repositories`, granted to planner and orchestrator in `src/core/authz.ts` and mapped in `src/core/commands/capabilities.ts`). It re-detects, appends new repositories, sets `missing: true` on vanished ones and clears it on returning ones, never removes an entry, appends the event `project.repositories_rescanned` with the added and missing names, and returns the new list. A single-repository project refuses it with `invalid_input`.
4. Register the MCP tool `rescan_repositories` (kind `idempotent`) in `src/mcp/tools/discovery.ts` next to `set_definition_of_done`, and add `rescanRepositories` to `DESKTOP_COMMANDS` in `src/shared/desktop/api.ts`.

**Out of scope**
Per-repository Definition of Done (DM-358) and the desktop set-up screen.

**Tests** (written first)
- `src/core/repo/initialize.test.ts`: a `multi_repo` set-up records `['alpha', 'beta']` in db mode and leaves the parent and both children unchanged (list them with modification times before and after); `mode: 'repo'`, a parent inside a Git repository and a parent without child repositories are each refused.
- `src/core/commands/repositories.test.ts` (new): rescan adds a new child, marks a removed one missing and keeps it, clears `missing` when it returns, and is refused for a single-repository project and for a reader.
- `src/core/repo/portable.test.ts`: a `project.json` without `repositories` parses and re-serializes byte-identical.

**Verify**
The listed tests, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: Touches the project record, set-up, authorization and a new command across core, MCP and desktop lists.

tickets.title: Set up a folder of repositories and record its repositories on the project

acceptanceCriteria.text: In a folder of repositories, adding a ticket with `repo: 'alpha'` and title `Add refund endpoint` stores `alpha - Add refund endpoint`, and a title that already has the prefix is not doubled.
Changing only the repository swaps the prefix, changing only the title keeps it, and clearing the repository leaves the bare description.
`repo` on an acceptance node, in a single-repository project, or naming an unlisted repository is refused with `invalid_input`.
A ticket without `repo` keeps its saved shape and hash, and the plan diff reports repository changes.
The listed tests pass, and lint and typecheck pass.

tickets.body:
**Context**
Ticket content is `ticketContent` and `ticketInput` in `src/core/schemas.ts`, mirrored by `TicketContent` in `src/shared/domain/bundle.ts`, and stored as JSON in `bundle_json`, so no SQL migration is needed. Every add and update passes through `buildTicket` (~136) and `patchTicket` (~183) in `src/core/plan/normalize.ts`, called from `applyDraftOps` in `src/core/plan/draftOps.ts` with the `DraftDeps` built by `draftDeps(ctx)` in `src/core/services/draftDeps.ts`. The MCP tools `create_ticket`, `update_ticket` and `update_plan_draft` reuse `ticketInput` (`src/mcp/tools/authoring.ts`), so they accept the field once the schema does. The project's repositories are `repositories` on the project record.

**Change**
1. `ticketContent` gains `repo?: string` (no default, like `size`, so saved tickets keep their shape and hash) and `ticketInput` gains `repo?: string | null` (`null` clears it in a patch). Add it to `TicketContent`.
2. New pure module `src/core/plan/repoTitles.ts`: `repoPrefix(repo)` returns `${repo} - `; `withRepoPrefix(repo, description)`; `descriptionOf(repo, title)` strips exactly that prefix when present.
3. `DraftDeps` gains `repositories(): string[] | null`: the project's repository names, or `null` for a single repository.
4. In `add_ticket` and `update_ticket` (through `buildTicket` and `patchTicket`):
   - Create with `repo` R and title T: the title becomes `withRepoPrefix(R, descriptionOf(R, T.trim()))`, so a title that already has R's prefix is not doubled.
   - Update: the description is `descriptionOf(oldRepo, patch.title ?? ticket.title)`; the title becomes the new repository's prefix plus that description, or the bare description when `repo` is cleared.
   - Refuse with `invalid_input`: `repo` on an acceptance node; `repo` in a single-repository project; a `repo` the project does not list (name the listed repositories); a prefixed title longer than `LIMITS.title`.
5. `src/core/plan/diff.ts`: the ticket change detail reports `repository A → B`.

**Out of scope**
Plan validation of missing repositories (next ticket) and UI.

**Tests** (written first)
- `src/core/plan/repoTitles.test.ts`: prefix, prefix not doubled, strip only the exact prefix (including a repository named `foo - bar` and a title that starts with another repository's prefix).
- `src/core/plan/draftOps.test.ts`: add with a repository; update the title only (prefix kept); update the repository only (prefix swapped); update both; clear the repository; each refusal above.
- `src/core/plan/normalize.test.ts`: a ticket without `repo` keeps its exact shape.
- `src/core/plan/diff.test.ts`: the repository change detail.

**Verify**
The listed tests, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: The prefix rules on update must hold for every combination of title and repository changes without changing saved hashes.

tickets.title: Give each ticket a target repository and keep its title prefixed

acceptanceCriteria.text: `validate_plan` reports `missing_repo`, `unknown_repo` and `repo_not_allowed` as errors and `repo_missing_on_disk` as a warning, each naming the ticket key and the repository.
`save_plan` refuses a plan with a repository error.
Single-repository plans validate exactly as before.
The listed tests pass, and lint and typecheck pass.

tickets.body:
**Context**
`validatePlan(bundle)` in `src/core/plan/graph.ts` (~503) is pure and returns `{ valid, errors, warnings }` from sub-checks such as `acceptanceErrors` (~382). Its callers are `src/core/services/drafts.ts` (~98), `src/core/services/plans.ts` (~224 `validatePlanView`, ~235 the save gate) and `src/core/services/redraft.ts` (~117). The draft-op checks of the previous ticket stop bad input; this rule catches plans that drifted afterwards: a repository marked missing by a rescan, or a work ticket never given a repository.

**Change**
- `validatePlan(bundle, options?: { repositories: RepositoryEntry[] | null })` with a new sub-check `repositoryIssues`:
  - error `missing_repo`: a work ticket in a folder of repositories has no `repo`;
  - error `unknown_repo`: a ticket names a repository the project does not list;
  - error `repo_not_allowed`: a ticket has `repo` in a single-repository project, or an acceptance node has `repo`;
  - warning `repo_missing_on_disk`: a ticket names a repository marked `missing`.
  Each issue names the ticket key and the repository.
- Pass the project's repositories from all four callers. Without options the function behaves exactly as today.

**Tests** (written first, in a new `src/core/plan/repositoryRules.test.ts` that follows `src/core/plan/acceptanceRules.test.ts`)
One case per issue code, a valid two-repository plan with no issue, and a single-repository plan without `repo` with no issue. One `src/core/services/plans.test.ts` case shows `save_plan` refuses a plan with `missing_repo`.

**Verify**
The listed tests, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: One pure sub-check with listed codes, threaded to four named callers.

tickets.title: Report missing and unknown ticket repositories in validate_plan and at save

acceptanceCriteria.text: The planner guide tells planners to set `repo` on every work ticket in a folder of repositories, to give titles without the prefix, and to split cross-repository changes into one ticket per repository.
The graph planner guide says covering criteria name the repository their check runs in.
`src/mcp/skills.test.ts` asserts the new rules and passes.

tickets.body:
**Context**
`skills/planner.md` and `skills/graph-planner.md` are served by the MCP server as prompts (`src/mcp/skills.ts`), with phrase assertions in `src/mcp/skills.test.ts`. After the previous tickets, `get_project` returns `repositories` for a folder of repositories, tickets take `repo`, and the server writes the `<repo> - ` title prefix.

**Change**
- `skills/planner.md`, section 4: add a short "Folders of repositories" rule. When `get_project` returns `repositories`, set `repo` on every work ticket to the repository it changes. One ticket changes one repository, so split a cross-repository change into one ticket per repository and wire them with dependencies. The server writes the `<repo> - ` prefix, so give the title without it. Acceptance nodes take no `repo`.
- `skills/graph-planner.md`, the acceptance node section: in a folder of repositories each covering criterion names the repository its check runs in.
- Keep all other text in both guides as it is.

**Tests**
Extend `src/mcp/skills.test.ts` to assert that the served planner prompt states the `repo` rule and the one-repository-per-ticket rule.

**Verify**
`npx vitest run src/mcp/skills.test.ts`, `npm run lint`.

reasoning.rationale: Guide text with the rules spelled out, plus one phrase test.

tickets.title: Teach the planner guides to target one repository per ticket

acceptanceCriteria.text: For a tracked folder that is not set up and not inside a Git repository, the folder view lists its child repositories; otherwise the list is null.
The set-up screen offers Folder of repositories only when child repositories exist, lists them, hides the `.mcp.json` option, and submits `{ mode: 'db', layout: 'multi_repo' }`.
Set-up for folders without child repositories is unchanged.
The listed tests pass, and lint and typecheck pass.

tickets.body:
**Context**
Set-up happens in `src/renderer/src/onboarding/OnboardingView.tsx` (`MODE_CHOICES` ~85, `StorageModeChoice` ~111, `SetupCard` ~296, tested by `OnboardingView.test.tsx`), which calls `repositoryActions.initialize` in `src/renderer/src/app/shellActions.ts` (`runCommand(folder.path, 'initializeRepository', { mode })`). The tracked folder view is `TrackedFolderView` (`src/shared/desktop/api.ts` ~11–22), built by `toView` in `src/main/desktop/folderRegistry.ts` (~147) through `RegistryFs` (~22–31), which has no `readdir` yet. `initialize_repository` accepts `layout: 'multi_repo'`, and `detectChildRepos` / `isInsideGitRepository` live in `src/core/repo/childRepos.ts`.

**Change**
1. Main: give `RegistryFs` (and its real implementation) `readdir` and `isSymlink`, and add `childRepositories: string[] | null` to `TrackedFolderView`. For a folder that is not set up and not inside a Git repository it is the result of `detectChildRepos`; otherwise it is `null`. Read nothing else.
2. Renderer: when `childRepositories` is non-empty, `SetupCard` offers a third choice, **Folder of repositories**, preselected when the folder is not itself a repository. It lists the detected repositories, says that plans live in this computer's Dark Mechanicus database and nothing is written into the folder or its repositories, and hides the `.mcp.json` option. Choosing it calls `initializeRepository` with `{ mode: 'db', layout: 'multi_repo' }`.
3. When `childRepositories` is empty or `null`, the screen is unchanged.

**Tests** (written first)
- `src/main/desktop/folderRegistry.test.ts`: a temp parent with two child repositories gives `childRepositories: ['alpha', 'beta']`; a repository folder and a set-up folder give `null`.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `gitFor(name)` returns an adapter rooted at that child repository, cached per name, and `gitFor(null)` returns the root adapter.

tickets.body:
**Context**
`RepositoryWorkspace` (`src/core/workspace.ts`) builds one adapter, `this.git = options.git ?? createGitAdapter(this.repoRoot, { fs })` (~153), exposed as `WorkspaceCore.git` (`src/core/commands/types.ts`) and passed to command contexts (~394). `createGitAdapter(root, { fs, runGit })` is in `src/core/repo/git.ts`. In a folder of repositories the root is not a repository, so `checkout()` (~325) sees no head. The project's repositories are `repositories` on the project record.

**Change**
- Add `gitFor(repo: string | null): GitAdapter` to `WorkspaceCore` and the command context. `null` returns the existing root adapter. A name:
  - must be listed in the project's `repositories` and not missing, else `invalid_input` naming it;
  - resolves `<root>/<name>` with `realpath` and is refused with `unsafe_path` unless it is not a symlink and its real path's parent is the real project root (no escape through `..`, separators or links);
  - returns an adapter cached per name, built with the same `createGitAdapter` options (tests may inject a factory, as `options.git` does today).
- Keep `core.git` as the root adapter; change no other call site in this ticket.
- Make sure `checkout()` and `assertBranch()` stay no-ops, without throwing, for a db-mode folder of repositories whose root has no `.git`.

**Tests** (written first)
`src/core/workspace.gitFor.test.ts` (new), with two real repositories made by `src/test/gitRepo.ts` under a temp parent: `gitFor('alpha').head()` reports alpha's branch and commit; `gitFor(null)` is the root adapter; an unlisted name, a missing one, `..`, `alpha/../beta` and a symlinked child are refused; the adapter is cached; opening the folder and reading its checkout does not throw.

**Verify**
The listed tests, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: Path containment for child repositories is security-relevant; a missed escape runs Git outside the folder.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Starting a run in a folder of repositories binds the shared branch name in every repository the saved plan's work tickets name, each with its own start commit.
Queueing or starting such a run without a branch name is refused with `invalid_input`.

tickets.body:
**Context**
`startRun` (`src/core/services/runs.ts` ~286) calls `bindEpicBranch` (~262), which binds once, from the request or from `checkoutBranch(ctx)` (~256: the root checkout's HEAD, `repository: null`). `setEpicBranch` (`src/core/services/epics.ts` ~339) sets it by hand. The epic stores `epics.branch_json`, exported as `epicStateRecord.branch` (`src/core/repo/portable.ts` ~97–115) and read into epic views. In a folder of repositories the root has no checkout, so the name must come from the epic or the request. `gitFor(repo)` gives each repository's adapter.

**Change**
1. Epics gain `repositoryBranches?: EpicBranch[]`. Store it either inside `branch_json` (then write a data-only V11 migration in `src/core/db/migrations.ts` following V10) or in a new column (then a V11 `ALTER TABLE` following V6); say which in the evidence. Mirror it in `epicStateRecord` (optional, no default) and the epic view.
2. In a folder of repositories:
   - `queue_run` and `start_run` refuse an epic with no branch name (`invalid_input`: set the epic branch first); `start_run`'s `branch` may supply it.
   - Binding sets `branch` to `{ repository: null, name, startCommit: null }` and binds each repository named by a work ticket of the saved revision being run as `{ repository: <name>, name, startCommit }`. `startCommit` is the commit of `refs/heads/<name>` in that repository when the branch exists, else that repository's HEAD commit. Add `branchCommit(name): string | null` to `GitAdapter` (`git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<name>^{commit}`, through `safeArg`) if no method gives it.
   - When the run adopts a later revision that names a new repository, bind that one then. Never rebind a bound repository.
   - Append `epic.branch_set` with the repositories bound.
3. Single-repository epics bind exactly as today.

**Tests** (written first)
`src/core/services/runs.test.ts`: a two-repository epic binds both with their own start commits (one with an existing branch, one from HEAD); a missing branch name is refused at queue and at start; a repository added in an adopted revision is bound, and a bound one keeps its commit; the existing single-repository cases pass unchanged. `src/core/repo/git.test.ts`: `branchCommit` for an existing and a missing branch, and `unsafe_path` for a leading dash.

**Verify**
The listed tests, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: Bind-once run state and a stored-shape migration; a wrong start commit silently breaks every later increment check.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An acceptance submission in a folder of repositories takes one increment per touched repository, and each is verified against that repository's Git history and previous increment.

tickets.body:
**Context**
`submit_attempt` (`src/core/commands/execution.ts` ~138) verifies `input.increment` through `verifiedIncrement` (~80–89): `incrementContextOf(ctx, attemptId)` (`src/core/services/increments.ts` ~70–90: `epicBranch`, `previous`, `workCommits`) and `verifyIncrement(core.git, context, named, verifiedAt)` (`src/core/services/incrementVerify.ts` ~227–255, which reads `refs/heads/<epic.name>` and checks the branch, reachability, base and squash). `storeSubmission` and `verdictOf` in `src/core/services/attempts.ts` (~489–563) store one verdict in `attempts.increment_json`. The input is `submitAttempt.increment: incrementRef.optional()` in `src/core/commandSchemas.ts`. `gitFor(repo)` and `repositoryBranches` exist.

**Change**
1. `incrementRef` gains `repo?: string`; `submitAttempt` gains `increments?: IncrementRef[]` (at most 100); the shared `IncrementRef` type follows.
2. In a folder of repositories an acceptance node's submission must use `increments`, with exactly one entry per touched repository. Refuse with `invalid_input` a singular `increment`, a missing touched repository, an untouched or unknown repository, and a duplicate. Single-repository projects refuse `increments` and are otherwise unchanged.
3. Verify each entry with `verifyIncrement(core.gitFor(repo), context, …)` against a per-repository context: that repository's bound `EpicBranch`; `previous` is its increment from the nearest earlier sprint whose standing acceptance attempt passed and touched it, else its start commit; `workCommits` are the accepted work commits of tickets with that `repo`. Give `incrementContextOf` a repository parameter rather than duplicating it, and take the touched repositories from `touchedRepositories(ctx, sprintId)`.
4. Store the verdicts as a JSON array in `attempts.increment_json`, each with its `repo`. Fail closed: one failed repository fails the node's increment.

**Tests** (written first)
`src/core/services/incrementVerify.test.ts` and `src/core/services/attemptsIncrement.test.ts`, with two real repositories from `src/test/gitRepo.ts`: both squashed increments pass; a merge commit in `beta` fails naming `beta`; a second sprint's increment is checked against that repository's previous increment; a repository untouched in sprint 1 is checked against its start commit in sprint 2; each refusal in step 2; the existing single-repository verification tests pass unchanged.

**Verify**
The listed tests, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: Verification must fail closed per repository; a wrong previous increment or work-commit set passes bad sprints.

tickets.body:
**Context**
The Definition of Done is one flat list in `project.json` (`definitionOfDone`), set by `set_definition_of_done` (planner-only capability `project.definition_of_done`; `writeDefinitionOfDone` in `src/core/repo/projectConfig.ts`), read by `ctx.definitionOfDone()` (`src/core/context.ts`), placed in acceptance packets by `definitionOfDonePart` (`src/core/services/attempts.ts` ~283–293), and enforced by the `definition_of_done` gate (`src/core/services/checkpoints.ts`, with `unmetChecks` in `src/core/definitionOfDone.ts`), which matches the node's `evidence.checks` by name. Acceptance packets in a folder of repositories already list `repositories`.

**Change**
- `RepositoryEntry` gains optional `definitionOfDone`. `set_definition_of_done` gains `repo?: string`: required in a folder of repositories, where it sets that repository's checks, and refused in a single-repository project. A folder of repositories has no folder-level list.
- Each `repositories` entry of an acceptance packet carries that repository's `definitionOfDone`.
- In a folder of repositories the node reports each check as `<repo>: <check name>`, and the `definition_of_done` gate checks every touched repository's list, naming unmet checks as `<repo>: <check> (<status>)`. A touched repository without a list adds no check.
- Update the MCP tool `set_definition_of_done` (`src/mcp/tools/discovery.ts`) input and description, and `DEFINITION_OF_DONE_INSTRUCTIONS` in `attempts.ts`.
Single-repository behavior is unchanged.

**Tests** (written first)

**Context**
`src/integration/incrementMerged.test.ts` and `src/integration/definitionOfDone.test.ts` drive whole runs against one real repository made with `src/test/gitRepo.ts` (`createGitRepo`, `squash`, `merge`, `branch`, `rev`) and the workspace harness (`src/test/workspaceHarness.ts`, `src/test/execution.ts`). **Change**
Add `src/integration/multiRepo.test.ts`, using a temp parent holding repositories `alpha` and `beta` and a temp `DARKMECHANICUS_HOME`:
1. Set up with `layout: 'multi_repo'` and set each repository's Definition of Done.
2. Create an epic with branch `feature` and one sprint with one work ticket per repository and a covering acceptance node; save; queue and start the run.

tickets.body:
**Context**
The role guides are `skills/orchestrator.md` (~20–58: `start_run` with a branch, a worktree per worker branched from the sprint integration branch, "Keep the coordinating checkout on the epic branch… `git -C <worktree>`", the acceptance round, the squash merge and `increment { branch, commit }`), `skills/worker.md` (~17, 26, 35), `skills/reviewer.md` (~18, 32) and `skills/sprint-reporter.md` (~18, 30, 31, 62–63). The MCP server serves them as prompts, and `src/main/agents/orchestratorKickoff.ts` embeds them in the desktop kickoff (`KickoffInput.branch`, `branchLine`, `HANDOFF`), which `src/main/agents/orchestratorStart.ts` feeds with `epic.branch?.name`. `src/mcp/skills.test.ts` (~186–190, 243–246) and `src/main/agents/orchestratorKickoff.test.ts` assert their text.

**Change**
Add a "Folders of repositories" paragraph to each guide and keep the single-repository text as it is:
- orchestrator: when a repository has no epic branch, create it at that repository's `startCommit` (`git -C <path> branch <name> <startCommit>`); never switch the branch of a child repository's own checkout (a folder of repositories has no branch guard), and keep the sprint integration branch, the workers' worktrees and the landing on the epic branch in worktrees per touched repository; give each worker a worktree of its packet's `repository.path`; squash each touched repository's sprint work onto its epic branch and submit `increments`, one per repository; give every ticket added in a retro redraft its `repo`.
- worker: work only in a worktree of `repository.path`, run Git as `git -C <worktree>`, and on an acceptance node report Definition of Done checks as `<repo>: <check>`.
- reviewer: diff against the integration branch in the ticket's repository; on an acceptance node expect one increment verdict and one set of checks per touched repository.
- sprint reporter: list each repository's increment commit and checks.
In the kickoff, `KickoffInput` takes `repositoryBranches` and `branchLine` lists `repository → branch` when they are present; `orchestratorStart` passes them from the epic.

**Tests** (written first)
`src/mcp/skills.test.ts`: the new rules in the served orchestrator and worker prompts. `src/main/agents/orchestratorKickoff.test.ts`: a two-repository epic's kickoff lists both branches, and a single-repository kickoff is unchanged.

**Verify**
The listed tests, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`.

**Context**
`docs/architecture.md` (~36–38: a Workspace per repository root; ~168–171: the project Definition of Done), `docs/product-plan.md` (~16: each repository owns its database; ~100–102: one feature branch per epic) and `docs/decisions/0002-storage-modes.md` describe one repository per folder. Runbooks live in `docs/runbooks/` and are linked from `README.md`.

**Change**
- New decision record `docs/decisions/0003-multi-repo-folders.md`: context; the decision (db mode only, immediate children, exact-name prefix kept by the server, one repository per work ticket, a shared branch name with per-repository start commits, per-repository increments and Definition of Done); consequences; known limits (a renamed child is marked missing, no Source control tab, nested repositories ignored).
- Update the architecture and product-plan lines above to cover folders of repositories.
- New runbook `docs/runbooks/multi-repo-folders.md`: set up, rescan, plan, run, and read per-repository results. Link it from `README.md` and `docs/runbooks/mcp-setup.md`.

**Tests**
None: documentation only.

**Verify**
`npm run lint`, and every relative link in the changed files resolves to an existing file.

reasoning.rationale: Documentation of decided behavior, with the files and lines named.
